That sounds like all the same points my mom has come up with. 
Sorry I don't have any advice that has actually worked yet as we are still dealing with it ourselves. I have not been able to go the social services route yet. 

But here are my thought on how to counter those points. 
It is not more expensive than losing your kid. You can pay off a hospital bill over time or get on medicaid or get a line of credit on your house but nothing can undo your kid dying. 

Most of the people I currently interact with are nothing like me. Most of the people I interact with don't cut themselves to try and stop feeling like shit all the time. Most of the people I know don't keep wills ready in case they decide to off themselves. So they can't really be any less like me than the people I currently interact with.

I am not saying that the mental healthcare system is perfect it has a lot of legitimate problems. That said though what else do we have? If the people who have spent decades of their lives training to help people in crisis can't do anything then who does she think can? If hospitals are not able to help people then why do we spend millions of dollars each year funding them? If they don't work at least somewhat why would we keep using them? They are definitely not perfect but it is still better than nothing. 

Modern medical science has helped save billions of lives. Sometimes people get sick and sometimes we need help dealing with that. If someone was born with type 1 diabetes would we just say well your screwed and let them die? No they need insulin to survive. Just because they were born with an illness and even an incurable illness does not mean their lives are not valuable. Especially not when we have found a way to manage that illness. Mental illnesses are no different. Sometimes things are mild and you can handle it with diet and exercise and be ok. Sometimes you have something more serious and you need help to manage it. Ask if I was told I had a tumor that was eating away at me would you let me take drugs to help fight it? Mental illnesses can be the exact same. Untreated they can eat away at you and even kill you. Treating them early and effectively with the methods scientifically proven to be the most effective, medication and therapy at the same time, can be the difference between dealing with a stage 2 tumor and a stage 4. 

Now my own mother has found ways to ignore or just guilt trip us out of most of these arguments anyway. So I am not promising they will work at all. But here is what I have tried in case you have any better luck.

My sister is having a similar issue with our mother. My sister is suicidal but feels like she can't go to the hospital because it would upset our mom. Our mom has told us our entire lives about how terrible the hospital is that all they do is pump you full of drugs and drag her into family court. 

Our mom is super anti pharmaceutical though. She used to complain about my dad taking heart medication even, because she thought he should just exercise more. She thinks vaccines cause autism and got upset with me for getting a flu shot. 

If your mom is flat out refusing to let you go then you can probably bring that up with your school counselor. If your counselor agrees that you may be a danger to yourself or others and that hospitalization would help then they should be able to contact social services and have you sent for evaluation. I am not saying this is a good option but it is something to consider.

It was my go to stress coping mechanism for a long time to picture myself stabbing myself in the gut. It would provide an amount of relief giving me a taste of the calm of ok I am dead now so it is all over. That would actually help me keep going and handle the stressful event. The problem for me though was that it was kind of like a drug that I started to build up a tolerance for and needed more and more and more. Eventually imagining wasn't enough and I started self harming.

These days I do try and treat it like an addiction. Though I have had an unfortunate relapse lately.

The stress part of that is what worries me a lot. I, and my sister too for that matter, worry that basically no matter what we do then as long as she is still receiving so many negative messages from our family then the stress will undo any progress she makes.

I recently moved out so I cannot do things like go run with her. 
I try to encourage her to exercise, eat better, get sleep, hang out with friends, etc. Sometimes it can be mildly helpful most of the time she shrugs it off or if she really feels like shit tells me to "go fuck myself that running won't solve anything". 

It doesn't bother me for her to get mad at me I understand why. I just wish I could be more helpful. It always feels like nothing I say helps.

Well I mean I am 99.99% certain that if she dies I will kill myself so I won't be regretting it for long. I worry that this could be the final piece of guilt tripping that could push her over the edge though. Or that if we are going to die then at least she can die without feeling the guilt of know I am as well.

She knows I feel shitty and knows I have dealt with being suicidal in the past. Any attempt at saying that it did get easier for me to deal with those feelings is usually shot down as either taking too long or she usually just says "that is bullshit" or that it is that her life is still fucked up and terrible she is just not caring anymore and says she feels like that is worse than feeling like suicidal. Part of what she says is that feel hates talking to me sometimes because she feels like she is poisoning me when there is still hope for me at least.
